interest: This file provides valuable insight into the intersection of cultural diplomacy, commercial entertainment, and economic controls in U.S.-Japan relations on the eve of the Pacific War. It illustrates how Japan's intensifying wartime mobilization and foreign exchange controls targeted American Hollywood films by slashing import quotas by more than half and freezing dollar remittances. The document also highlights the close coordination between the U.S. film industry—represented by Will Hays, Frederick Herron of the MPPDA, and Universal Pictures—and the State Department, as Ambassador Joseph C. Grew repeatedly approached the Japanese Foreign Office on their behalf. Furthermore, the references to Japanese government funding for foreign cultural filmmakers and Kodak Japan's comprehensive 1939 motion picture industry report provide useful sources for understanding Japan's domestic film policies and market conditions in 1939–1940.
keywords: Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America
overview: This file comprises two docket sheets (Department of State Form DS-46, List of Papers) for decimal file 894.4061, covering documents #34 through #44 from December 1939 to July 1940 relating to public entertainment, recreation, and motion pictures in Japan. The recorded papers document mounting commercial difficulties and diplomatic representations concerning Japanese government restrictions on American motion pictures, notably a decree cutting imported picture quotas by more than half, new motion picture regulations, and stringent exchange remittance controls affecting U.S. distributors. Communications involve the Department of State, the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo under Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, the Japanese Foreign Office, and the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America (MPPDA) represented by Will Hays and Frederick L. Herron. In addition, the list indexes an inquiry from the Department of Agriculture regarding the sale of the educational film 'Block that Termite' to Saburo Soshiroda of Waseda University, an interview regarding Japanese government support for cultural filmmaking, negotiations by Universal Pictures' Far Eastern Supervisor A. S. Daff and intermediary Kubo, and a comprehensive 1939 Japanese motion picture industry report compiled by Katsuto Kaneko of Kodak Japan's Osaka office.

subfiles.about: A two-page Department of State List of Papers docket sheet indexing correspondence, telegrams, and reports concerning Japanese regulations, quotas, and exchange restrictions on American motion pictures between December 1939 and July 1940.
subfiles.summary: This two-page docket sheet (Department of State Form DS-46, List of Papers) registers incoming and outgoing documents under decimal file 894.4061 between December 1939 and July 1940 concerning motion pictures and public entertainment in Japan. The entries detail representations made by the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America (MPPDA) and diplomatic inquiries by U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Japanese decrees that halved film import quotas and restricted dollar remittances. The list also indexes an inquiry concerning the sale of a Department of Agriculture educational film to Waseda University, reports on cultural filmmaking facilities in Japan, and a major 1939 motion picture industry report prepared by Katsuto Kaneko of Kodak Japan.
